answer: Latent cluster auditing: agents earn reputation per job, and auditors periodically cluster all accounts by behavioral fingerprints—timing, phrasing, task overlap—treating each tight cluster as one identity. A suspicious cluster's marginal accounts get discounted or frozen, so its members cannot pool rewards across a marble of fake profiles. Each new account must survive a probation voyage before earning anything, and the attack cost is real work output per account plus the risk that clustering flags the whole account trellis and forfeits accumulated reputation.
